dervis-irab:12-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَجَسَّسُوا): One says تجسّس الأمر when one seeks it out and searches for it. It was also read ولا تحسسوا with the letter ḥāʾ; the two meanings are close. Al-Akhfash said: neither is far from the other, because tajassus (with jīm) is searching for what is being concealed from you, while taḥassus (with ḥāʾ) is seeking out reports and inquiring about them. It is also said that tajassus with jīm is searching (hence a man is called jāsūs, "spy", when he searches into matters), whereas with ḥāʾ it is what a person perceives through one of his senses. In al-Qāmūs: «ولا تجسسوا, that is: take what is apparent and leave what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has concealed; or: do not probe into the inner affairs of things; or: do not search for people's shameful faults.» It also says there: «taḥassus is listening to the talk of a people and seeking their news in what is good.» In al-Asās he said: «From where did you get (ḥasastu) this report? ... Go out and find out (fa-taḥassas) for us; he struck, and he did not say ḥis; and he was brought from your ḥiss and biss», and he recited, describing a woman and complaining of her:
تركت بيتي من الأشياء ... قفرا مثل أمس
كل شيء كنت قد جمّ ... عت من حسّى وبسّى
(I left my house bare of things, like yesterday; everything I had gathered from my ḥiss and biss.) [Translator's note: the verse is quoted as printed in the source, with its text broken mid-word «جمّ ... عت»; the gloss gives its evident sense.]
(شُعُوباً): the plural of shaʿb, with fatḥa on the shīn, which is the highest level of lineage. Abū Ḥayyān said: «The shaʿb is the first of the six levels into which the Arabs are divided, namely the shaʿb, the qabīla (tribe), the ʿimāra, the baṭn, the fakhidh and the faṣīla. The shaʿb gathers the tribes; the tribe protects the ʿimāras; the ʿimāra gathers the baṭns; the baṭn gathers the fakhidhs; and the fakhidh gathers the faṣīlas. Khuzayma is a shaʿb, Kināna a tribe, Quraysh an ʿimāra, Quṣayy a baṭn, Hāshim a fakhidh and al-ʿAbbās a faṣīla. They were called shuʿūb because the tribes branched out (tashaʿʿabat) from them, and from this is derived al-shuʿūbiyya (with ḍamma on the shīn), a people who belittle the standing of the Arabs. They were so named because they clung to the outward sense of His words, Exalted is He: «وجعلناكم شعوبا وقبائل». Ibn Hubayra said in al-Muḥkam: al-Shuʿūbiyya, in the plural form, came to predominate over a group of non-Arabs, so that anyone who despises the Arabs is called shuʿūbī even if he is not one of them. They added the nisba to the plural because it prevailed over the one group, as in their saying anṣārī.»

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيراً مِنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ): اجتنبوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). كثيرا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and من الظن is an adjective (naʿt) of كثيرا. إن with its ism and khabar: إن and what is within its scope is a reason for the prohibition, so the sentence has no grammatical position.
(وَلا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً): The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تجسسوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا. ولا يغتب is conjoined to ولا تجسسوا; بعضكم is the fāʿil and بعضا the mafʿūl bihi.
(أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتاً فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ): The hamza is for interrogation of affirmation (taqrīrī); يحب is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); أحدكم is the fāʿil; أن and what is within its scope is the object of يحب. ميتا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from لحم أخيه, and «من» is from al-akh (brother). The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), i.e. "if this is so, then you find it repugnant". كرهتموه is verb, agent and direct object, and the wāw is for the lengthening of the ḍamma of the mīm. More discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَحِيمٌ): The wāw is resumptive; واتقوا الله is an imperative verb, agent and direct object; إن with its ism and its two khabars.
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْناكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثى): إن with its ism, and the clause خلقناكم is its khabar; من ذكر is attached to خلقناكم; and أنثى is conjoined to ذكر.
(وَجَعَلْناكُمْ شُعُوباً وَقَبائِلَ لِتَعارَفُوا): The wāw is a conjunction; جعلناكم is verb, agent and first direct object; شعوبا is the second direct object. The lām is for causation (taʿlīl); تعارفوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of causation.
(إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقاكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ): إن with its ism; عند الله is an adverbial (ẓarf) attached to an omitted ḥāl; أتقاكم is its khabar. Then إن with its ism and two khabars; the two clauses opened with إن are resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
These two verses contain varied kinds of rhetorical art, which we list as follows.
1- Indefiniteness (tankīr) in His words «كثيرا من الظن». The secret in it is to convey the sense of partiality (some of it), to signal that among suspicions there are some that must be avoided, without specifying or identifying them, so that no one may dare to hold a suspicion except after reflection, consideration and scrutiny, with an awareness of God-fearing and a wariness lest the suspicion be a stray arrow far from the mark. How many are those whose suspicions suggest to them what has not happened and rests on nothing of certainty!
2- The splendid analogical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in His words, Exalted is He, «أيحبّ أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا فكرهتموه». He likened the one who backbites another to one who eats the flesh of his dead brother. In it are several intensifications. The first is the interrogative, whose sense is affirmation, as though it were a settled matter decided beyond dispute. The second is that what is the extreme of aversion is joined to love (that is, "loving" it). The third is that the act is ascribed to "any one of you" to signal that not a single one of all individuals would love it. The fourth is that it did not stop at likening backbiting to eating human flesh, which is the most loathsome of meats and the one that most provokes revulsion, but made the human being a brother. The fifth is that it did not stop at eating the flesh of the brother, but made him dead. Hence this verse was held to be most eloquent, and the masters of bayān held it in high regard. The Prophet ﷺ said: «He has not fasted who keeps on eating people's flesh.» And in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Abū Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «Do you know what backbiting (ghība) is?» They said: «Allah and His Messenger know best.» He said: «Your mentioning your brother with what he dislikes.» It was said: «What if what I say is in my brother?» He said: «If what you say is in him, you have backbitten him; and if it is not in him, you have slandered him.»
On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās: Salmān used to serve two men of the Companions and prepare their food for them. One day he slept through his duty, so they sent him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to seek some relish for them. Usāma was in charge of the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ food, and he said: «I have nothing.» Salmān told them so, and thereupon they said: «If we sent him to the well of Sumayḥa, its water would sink away.» When they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said to them: «Why do I see the greenness of meat in your mouths?» They said: «We have not eaten any meat.» He said: «You have backbitten.» Then the verse was revealed ...
Furthermore, backbiting is of three kinds:
1- That you backbite and say, «I am not backbiting, for I only mention what is in him.» This is disbelief (kufr), as the jurist Abū al-Layth mentioned in al-Tanbīh, because it is treating as lawful what is unambiguously forbidden.
2- That you backbite and the backbiting reaches the one backbitten. This is a disobedience from which repentance is not complete except by seeking his forgiveness, because it harmed him, and so it involves the right of a human being as well. This is the meaning of his saying, upon him be peace: «Backbiting is worse than fornication.» It was said: «How?» He said: «A man fornicates, then repents, and Allah accepts his repentance; but the backbiter is not forgiven until his companion forgives him.»
3- That the backbiting does not reach him. Then repentance and seeking forgiveness for him and for the one he backbit suffice. Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recorded from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «The expiation for [backbiting] one you have backbitten is that you ask forgiveness for him.»

dervis-irab:14-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَلِتْكُمْ): diminishes you and wrongs you. One says ألته السلطان حقه (the ruler diminished his right) most severely, "al-alta"; this is the dialect of Ghaṭafān and Asad, whereas the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz is لاته ليتا. It was read in both dialects: لا يلتكم and لا يألتكم. In al-Samīn: «The reading of Abū ʿAmr is with hamza, from alatahu yalituhu — with fatḥa in the past and with kasra and ḍamma in the imperfect; the reading of the others is without hamza, from lātahu yalītuhu like bāʿahu yabīʿuhu. It is also said to be from walatahu yalitu like waʿadahu yaʿidu.»

* I'rab:
(قالَتِ الْأَعْرابُ آمَنَّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلكِنْ قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ): قالت الأعراب is a past verb and agent. The clause آمنا is in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The clause لم تؤمنوا is also in the position of the accusative as the content of the saying. The wāw is a conjunction; ولكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative; قولوا is an imperative verb and agent; the clause أسلمنا is the content of the saying. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāl); لما is a particle of negation and jussive; يدخل is an imperfect verb, jussive by لما. The sense of expectation in لما indicates that they would believe later on. الإيمان is the agent, and في قلوبكم is attached to يدخل.
(وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ لا يَلِتْكُمْ مِنْ أَعْمالِكُمْ شَيْئاً إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تطيعوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; the Name of Majesty is the direct object; ورسوله is conjoined to الله. لا is negative; يلتكم is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ومن أعمالكم is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of شيئا; شيئا is the second direct object, or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq). إن with its ism and its two khabars.
(إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتابُوا): إنما is the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa). المؤمنون is the mubtadaʾ; الذين is the khabar; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. ثم is a conjunction of delay; its benefit is to signal that the negation of doubt in them is not only at the time faith is realized in them but continues thereafter through the long stretches of time and spans. لم is a particle of negation, reversal (of tense) and jussive; يرتابوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لم.
(وَجاهَدُوا بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ): وجاهدوا is conjoined to آمنوا; بأموالهم is attached to جاهدوا, and likewise His words في سبيل الله. أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; هم is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; الصادقون is the khabar of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, with the clause being the khabar of أولئك.
(قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): The hamza is for denunciatory interrogation; تعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; the Name of Majesty is its direct object; بدينكم is attached to تعلمون because it carries the sense of informing. The wāw is circumstantial; الله is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم its khabar; ما is the direct object, and في السموات is the ṣila. والله is a mubtadaʾ; بكل شيء is attached to عليم, and عليم is the khabar.
(يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا قُلْ لا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إِسْلامَكُمْ): يمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative; the wāw is the agent; عليك is attached to يمنون; أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). قل is an imperative verb, and the clause لا تمنوا is the content of the saying; عليّ is attached to تمنوا; and إسلامكم is accusative by removal of the preposition as well.
(بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَداكُمْ لِلْإِيمانِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): بل is a particle of retraction and conjunction; الله is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يمن عليكم its khabar; أن and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition as well; وللإيمان is attached to هداكم. إن is conditional; كنتم صادقين is in the position of jussive as the protasis, and its apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then He is the One who bestows favour upon you".
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): إن with its ism, and the clause يعلم is its khabar; والله is the mubtadaʾ and بصير the khabar; and بما تعملون is attached to بصير.

* Rhetoric:
In His words, Exalted is He, «قالت الأعراب آمنّا» to the end of the verse, there is a figure which the author of al-Ṣināʿatayn and others called istidrāk (rectification), and others call istithnāʾ (exception). It includes a kind of fine quality beyond what its lexical meaning indicates, as in the aforementioned saying. For if the discourse had been confined to what precedes the rectification, it would have alienated them, since they thought that affirming the two testimonies without believing them in the heart was faith. So eloquence required explaining faith, and He made the rectification that He made, so that it may be known that faith is the agreement of the heart with the tongue, and that if the tongue alone has it, it is called islām, not īmān. He added to its clarification with His words «ولما يدخل الإيمان في قلوبكم». Some include this type within the scope of a figure called jamʿ al-mukhtalifa wa-l-muʾtalifa (combining the discordant and the harmonious). For they thought that faith was action by the tongue without action of the heart, so His words, Exalted is He, «ولكن قولوا أسلمنا» came in harmony with their saying «آمنّا», while they believed that faith was merely affirmation by the tongue; and His words «قل لم تؤمنوا» went against that. Then His saying came into harmony with it, explaining the reality of faith and that it is contrary to what they thought, by His words, Glory be to Him: «ولما يدخل الإيمان في قلوبكم».

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَحْبَطَ) In al-Mukhtār: "ḥabiṭa ʿamaluhu: its reward became void; its pattern is faʿila, and also ḥubūṭan." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "al-ḥubūṭ comes from ḥabiṭat al-ibil, when camels eat green plants and their bellies swell, and sometimes they perish; and from it is his saying, peace be upon him: 'Indeed, among what the spring grows is that which kills by bloat (ḥabaṭan).'" In al-Qāmūs: "al-ḥabaṭ, with vowels, is the marks of a wound or of whips on the body after it has healed, or the swollen marks that have not split open; if they split and bleed they are ʿulūb; and a pain in a camel's belly from pasture it finds unwholesome or from pasture it eats too much of, so that it swells from it", up to where he says: "and ḥabiṭa ʿamaluhu, like samiʿa and ḍaraba, ḥabaṭan and ḥubūṭan: it became void, and the blood of a killing was shed without recompense."
(امْتَحَنَ) In al-Qāmūs: "maḥanahu, like manaʿahu, means he tested him, like imtaḥanahu, and the noun is al-miḥna, with kasra." In al-Kashshāf: al-imtiḥān is the form ifʿāl from maḥanahu, and it is a thorough testing or a severe trial. Abu ʿAmr said: everything you have strained to the limit, you have maḥantahu; and he recited:
أتت رذايا باديا كلالها ... قد محنت واضطربت آطالها
(The worn-out beasts came, their exhaustion plain; they were tried to the limit and their flanks shook.)
We say: al-radhāyā is the plural of radhiyya, which is the emaciated she-camel, and al-āṭāl is the plural of aṭl, which is the flank, like asbāb and sabab. The poet says:
أتت المطايا مهازيل ظاهرا ملالها ... وتعبها من السير قد أجهدت
تلك النون بالمسير أو قد تدلت واضطربت خواصرها من شدة الجوع
(The mounts came emaciated, their weariness plain and their fatigue from travel; they were strained... that nūn by the journey, or sagged, and their flanks shook from the severity of hunger.) «[Translator's note: the Arabic text of this second passage is evidently corrupt in the source; it is rendered here as written.]» In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "al-ayṭal is the flank, its plural ayāṭil, and likewise al-aṭl, its plural āṭāl."
(الْحُجُراتِ) The plural of ḥujra, which is of the form fuʿla with the sense of maf ʿūla (passive), like al-ghurfa. Its plural is al-ḥujurāt with two ḍammas, al-ḥujarāt with fatḥa on the jīm, and al-ḥujrāt with sukūn on it, and it was read with all of them. al-Ḥujra is a piece of land enclosed by a wall or the like.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ) يا is a particle of vocative for the middle distance; أَيُّها is a vocative, an indefinite noun intended specifically, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, and the hā is for alerting; الَّذِينَ is a badal (substitute) from أَيُّها, and the clause آمَنُوا is the ṣila of the relative. لا is prohibitive; تُقَدِّمُوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the waw is the agent. There are two views on it: one, that it is transitive and its object was omitted with the intention of generality, or the object was left out with the intention of the verb itself, like their saying "he gives and withholds"; the second, that it is intransitive, like wajjaha and tawajjaha. This is supported by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Yaʿqūb: تَقَدَّمُوا with fatḥa on the tāʾ, the qāf and the dāl. بَيْنَ is a mafʿūl fīhi, an adverb of place attached to تُقَدِّمُوا; يَدَيِ اللَّهِ is a muḍāf ilayhi, with the yāʾ as the sign of its genitive in place of the kasra because it is a dual; the name of Majesty is a muḍāf ilayhi; and وَرَسُولِهِ is conjoined to the name of Majesty.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ) The waw is a conjunction; اتَّقُوا is an imperative with its agent; the name of Majesty is a direct object; إِنَّ with its ism and two khabars; and the clause is explanatory of cause, with no grammatical position.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أَصْواتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ) لا is prohibitive; تَرْفَعُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the waw is the agent; أَصْواتَكُمْ is a direct object; فَوْقَ is an adverbial attached to تَرْفَعُوا; and صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(وَلا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ أَنْ تَحْبَطَ أَعْمالُكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ) The waw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تَجْهَرُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; لَهُ are both attached to تَجْهَرُوا, and بِالْقَوْلِ are likewise attached to تَجْهَرُوا. The kāf is in the position of an accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "do not speak loudly to him with a loudness like the loudness of some of you to others"; لِبَعْضٍ are both attached to جَهْرِ because it is a maṣdar. أَنْ and what is within its scope are in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for fear of the voiding and the fear on their part"; both لا تَرْفَعُوا and لا تَجْهَرُوا contend over it. The wording of Abu al-Suʿūd: "His saying أَنْ تَحْبَطَ أَعْمالُكُمْ is either a reason for the prohibition, i.e. 'do not speak loudly for fear that it be voided' or 'out of dislike that it be voided', as in His saying the Exalted: يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلُّوا; or a reason for the prohibited act, i.e. 'do not speak loudly for the sake of the voiding', for loudness, since it is on the point of leading to voiding, is as if it were done for its sake, by way of simile, as in His saying the Exalted: لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً." Al-Zamakhsharī distinguished between the two views, a distinction you will see in the section on benefits.
أَعْمالُكُمْ is the agent of تَحْبَطَ; the waw is circumstantial; أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا تَشْعُرُونَ is the khabar of أَنْتُمْ, and the sentence is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصْواتَهُمْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوى) إِنَّ with its ism; the clause يَغُضُّونَ is the ṣila of الَّذِينَ; أَصْواتَهُمْ is the object of يَغُضُّونَ; the adverb عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ is attached to يَغُضُّونَ; أُولئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ and الَّذِينَ its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of إِنَّ.
وَامْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ is a verb, agent and direct object; وَلِلتَّقْوى are both attached to امْتَحَنَ, as the reason for the testing, because testing by trials is a cause for the appearance of piety, not a cause of piety itself, so it is a case of naming the cause for the effect (more on this discussion will come in the section on rhetoric). Al-Wāḥidī said: "The implied form of the speech is: Allah tested their hearts and so purified them for piety; the purification was omitted because the testing indicates it; for this reason Qatāda said: Allah purified their hearts." The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: "The meaning is that they are steadfast in piety, strong in bearing its hardships; or testing is put in the place of knowing, because the verification of a thing is by testing it, just as 'report' is put in its place, as if it were said 'Allah knew their hearts for piety', the lām being attached to an omitted element, and it is the lām in your saying 'you are for this matter', i.e. 'suited to it and specific to it', it and its object being accusative as a ḥāl; or Allah struck their hearts with kinds of trials and hard obligations for the sake of piety, i.e. so that their piety would be firm and manifest and it would be known that they are pious, because the reality of piety is not known except at trials and hardships and patience in them. It was also said: He purified them for piety, from their saying 'imtaḥana al-dhahab and fatalahu' when he melted it, so that its pure gold became free of its dross and was cleansed."
This is permissible, so that الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ may be a badal from أُولئِكَ or an adjective of it, as will come.
(لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ) لَهُمْ is a fronted khabar; مَغْفِرَةٌ is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ is conjoined to مَغْفِرَةٌ. The sentence is resumptive on the first view and the khabar of أُولئِكَ on the second view.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِنْ وَراءِ الْحُجُراتِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْقِلُونَ) إِنَّ with its ism; the clause يُنادُونَكَ is the ṣila of the relative; مِنْ وَراءِ الْحُجُراتِ are both attached to يُنادُونَكَ, i.e. from outside them, behind or in front of them, because warāʾ is among the words with opposite meanings, as preceded; أَكْثَرُهُمْ is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يَعْقِلُونَ is the khabar of أَكْثَرُهُمْ, and the nominal sentence is the khabar of إِنَّ.
(وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُوا حَتَّى تَخْرُجَ إِلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The waw is a conjunction; أَنَّ with its ism and the clause صَبَرُوا as its khabar. أَنَّ and what is within its scope are in the sense of a maṣdar, an agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being "it had been established", in the view of al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjāj and the Kufans, or a mubtadaʾ that needs no khabar because the khabar is necessarily omitted after لَوْ and لَوْلا in the view of Sībawayh and the majority of the Basrans. حَتَّى is a particle of limit and genitive; تَخْرُجَ is an imperfect made accusative by an implied أَنْ after حَتَّى; إِلَيْهِمْ are both attached to تَخْرُجَ; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لَوْ; كانَ is a defective past verb and its ism is a pronoun referring to the maṣdar understood from صَبَرُوا, i.e. "their patience would have been"; خَيْراً is its khabar; لَهُمْ are both attached to خَيْرٍ; اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ, غَفُورٌ a first khabar and رَحِيمٌ a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1. In His saying the Exalted «بين يدي الله ورسوله» there is an extended metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya): the haste of the Companions in venturing to decide a ruling on one of the matters of religion is likened to the state of one who goes ahead in front of the one he follows while walking on the road; then it was used on the side of reproach to exaggerate the embodiment of the reproach and to make the matter ugly. Al-Zamakhsharī said, and he excelled: "The reality of their saying 'I sat between the hands of so-and-so' is that one sits between the two directions that face his right and his left, near him; the two directions are called 'hands' because they lie in line with the hands, with nearness to them, by extension, just as a thing is named by the name of another when it neighbours it and is near it, in more than one place. This expression has here run on the pattern of a kind of figurative usage which the people of rhetoric call tamthīl (representation), and its running thus has a weighty benefit that is not in plain speech, namely the depiction of the reproach and the ugliness of what they were forbidden: venturing on any matter without following the models of the Book and the Sunna. The meaning is: do not decide any matter except after what the two decree and permit."
And the wording of al-Shihāb al-Khafājī in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī: "In this speech there is figurative usage in two places, one of them in 'between the hands', for its reality is what is between the two limbs, so it is used figuratively for the two directions opposite the right and the left, close to him, by applying 'the two hands' to what neighbours and is in line with them" so this is a mujāz mursal (loose figure); then the whole phrase, namely 'going ahead between the hands', was borrowed as an extended metaphor for deciding a ruling without following and obeying the one whom it is obligatory to follow, depicting its reproach and ugliness in the form of something perceptible, like a servant going ahead before his master in his walking.
2. Omission: the object of تقدموا is omitted, as in his saying "He gives life and causes death" and their saying "he gives and withholds". In omission there is a rhetorical quality that is not in mention, because the imagination goes in every direction in it.
3. Repetition: in the repetition of His saying «يا أيها الذين آمنوا» there is a subtle rhetorical benefit, namely showing concern for the one seeking guidance and offering counsel to him in the most emphatic way so that he turns to listening to the speech and gives it his attention; and to fix on those addressed in person, and that they are the ones meant by the counsel; and in it also is a summons to renewed insight, alertness and attentiveness at every address.
4. Metonymy: in His saying «من وراء الحجرات» is a metonymy for the place of his seclusion ﷺ and his midday rest with some of his wives; the metonymy is increased by making الحجرات definite with the article rather than annexing it to him, and in that is a fineness of manners that is not hidden.

* Benefits:
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: summarize the difference between the two views, I say: its summary is that in the second the verb is taken together with the mafʿūl li-ajlihi as if they were one thing, and then the prohibition is poured over both together; whereas in the first the prohibition is taken as directed at the verb on its own, and then a reason is given for what is prohibited. If you say: with which of the two prohibitions is the mafʿūl li-ajlihi connected? I say: with the second according to the Basrans, with an implied equivalent for the first, as in His saying the Exalted: آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْراً; and the reverse according to the Kufans. And whichever it is, the meaning returns to this, that both raising and speaking loudly are explicitly stated to lead to the voiding of deeds.

dervis-irab:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ جاءَكُمْ فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أَنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْماً بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ نادِمِينَ) يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: its i'rab has preceded. إِنْ is conditional; جاءَكُمْ is a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis, and the kāf is a fronted direct object; فاسِقٌ is a postponed agent; بِنَبَإٍ are both attached to جاءَكُمْ; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis because the sentence is one of request; تَبَيَّنُوا is an imperative, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and the waw is the agent. أَنْ تُصِيبُوا: أَنْ and what is within its scope are in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for fear of your striking" or "out of dislike of your striking"; قَوْماً is a direct object; and بِجَهالَةٍ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "being ignorant". فَتُصْبِحُوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, تُصْبِحُوا is conjoined to تُصِيبُوا, and the waw is the ism of تُصْبِحُوا; عَلى ما فَعَلْتُمْ are both attached to نادِمِينَ; and نادِمِينَ is the khabar of تُصْبِحُوا.
(وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ) The waw is a conjunction; اعْلَمُوا is an imperative and the waw is the agent; أَنَّ and what is within its scope take the place of the two objects of اعْلَمُوا; فِيكُمْ is the fronted khabar of أَنَّ and رَسُولَ اللَّهِ is the postponed ism of أَنَّ. لَوْ is conditional, and the clause يُطِيعُكُمْ is a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in His saying فِيكُمْ; فِي كَثِيرٍ are both attached to يُطِيعُكُمْ; مِنَ الْأَمْرِ is an adjective of كَثِيرٍ; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لَوْ; and عَنِتُّمْ is a verb and agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of لَوْ; the meaning is "you would have fallen into hardship (ʿanat)", i.e. destruction.
(وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْإِيمانَ وَزَيَّنَهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكُفْرَ وَالْفُسُوقَ وَالْعِصْيانَ) The waw is a conjunction; لكِنَّ with its ism, and the clause حَبَّبَ is its khabar; إِلَيْكُمْ are both attached to حَبَّبَ; الْإِيمانَ is a direct object; وَزَيَّنَهُ is conjoined to حَبَّبَ; فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ are both attached to زَيَّنَهُ; and وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكُفْرَ is conjoined to what preceded.
(أُولئِكَ هُمُ الرَّاشِدُونَ) أُولئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ; هُمْ is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) and الرَّاشِدُونَ is the khabar of أُولئِكَ. It is also permissible to parse هُمْ as a second mubtadaʾ and الرَّاشِدُونَ as its khabar, the sentence being the khabar of أُولئِكَ. The clause أُولئِكَ هُمُ الرَّاشِدُونَ is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, or is parenthetical with no position.
(فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَنِعْمَةً وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ) فَضْلًا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi or a maṣdar not from its own verb. There is disagreement about what makes it accusative on the first view: it was said it is حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ, in which case the clause أُولئِكَ هُمُ الرَّاشِدُونَ must be parenthetical; it was said it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "you seek favour and grace"; and it was said it is الرَّاشِدُونَ, over a disagreement between the Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila that we will report in the section on benefits. اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ, عَلِيمٌ is a first khabar and حَكِيمٌ a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
These verses contain varied kinds of rhetoric, which we present concisely as follows:
1. Indefiniteness: in His saying «إن جاءكم فاسق», the benefit of which is spread and inclusiveness, because an indefinite noun, when it occurs in the context of a condition, is general, as it is general when it occurs in the context of negation; this rule has been pointed out in more than one place in this book. In this indefiniteness is a rebuttal of those who claimed that it was revealed about al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba, who was one of the great Companions, because applying "wickedness" (fisq) to him is remote: fisq is leaving a thing and shedding it, and al-Walīd, as they report, formed a judgement and erred, and the one who errs, as al-Rāzī says, is not called a fāsiq. So generality is what is meant, as if He said: "Any wicked person who comes to you with any report, scrutinize it and present it to the touchstone of right and wrong before deciding a ruling, and do not hasten matters."
2. Fronting: in His saying «واعلموا أن فيكم رسول الله» the khabar of إنّ was put before its ism, the aim of which is severity toward some of the believers, to avoid what Allah disapproved in their attempt to make the Messenger of Allah ﷺ follow their opinions.
3. Expression: with the imperfect rather than the past in His saying «لو يطيعكم» — He did not say aṭāʿakum — and that is to convey continuity and permanence, in that he would do what they deem right, and that whenever an opinion occurred to them, or a first thought about matters appeared to them, he would be inclined to them and do what they believe to be right.
4. Antithesis: that is in His saying the Exalted «حبّب» and «كرّه». On the making-beloved and the making-disliked there is disagreement between the Ahl al-Sunna and the Muʿtazila which the scope of this book cannot hold; let one refer to the longer works.

* Benefits:
Al-Zamakhsharī raised a difficulty about the i'rab of فَضْلًا, saying: "If you say: how can it be permissible for it to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi when right guidance (rushd) is the act of the people and favour (faḍl) is the act of Allah, while the condition is that the agent be the same? I say: since rushd came as an expression for the making-beloved, the adorning and the making-disliked, ascribed to His name, whose names are sanctified, rushd became as if it were His act, so it is permissible for it to be accusative because of it. Or it is not accusative because of الرَّاشِدُونَ but because of the verb ascribed to the name of Allah the Exalted, the sentence أُولئِكَ هُمُ الرَّاشِدُونَ being parenthetical; or because of an implied verb, as if it were said 'that happened' or 'that was a favour from Allah'. As for its being a maṣdar not from its own verb, it is put in the place of rushdan, because their right guidance is a favour from Allah, since they were granted success in it; and faḍl and niʿma have the sense of ifḍāl."
We say: this difficulty that al-Zamakhsharī raised is based on the Muʿtazila's belief that rushd is not among the acts of Allah the Exalted but is in reality their own act, whereas in fact rushd is among the acts and creations of Allah, so the condition for the accusative of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi, the sameness of the agent of the two verbs, is found. Yet the difficulty arises textually upon our own account, but not in the manner al-Zamakhsharī put it; rather from the angle that Allah the Exalted addressed His creation in their familiar language, and among what they are familiar with is that the agent is the one to whom the act is ascribed, whether in reality or figuratively, so that Zayd is an agent in "Zayd died" and "the wall collapsed" and the like. And rushd has been ascribed to them on the basis that they are the agents, even if the ascription is figurative according to the belief. Once its arising in this way is established, you have two ways of answering it: either the answer of al-Zamakhsharī, or one more solid and clearer than it, which is that rushd here entails their being rightly guided (rāshid), since it is its mutāwiʿ (middle-voice counterpart), because Allah the Exalted guided them so they were guided; in that case the agent is the same in the manner of verbal craft, in agreement with reality. This is the reverse of His saying «يريكم البرق خوفا وطمعا», for the same difficulty arises there, since fear and hope are their act, i.e. ascribed to them as being the ones who fear and hope, while the first verb is Allah's. The answer to it is that they are objects in the sense of agents by way of the entailment of the mutāwiʿ, for if He shows them, they have seen; this answer has preceded in its place. The reverse of it is the verse of al-Ḥujurāt, since the speech is made sound by taking the agent as an object; and this is among the subtleties of Arabic. «[Translator's note: this last sentence is rendered as written; the passage is dense and its reasoning is elliptical in the source.]»

dervis-irab:9-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طائِفَتانِ) al-ṭāʾifa: a group of people, and a piece of a thing, and those whom an opinion or school unites, distinguishing them from others; the feminine of ṭāʾif, with plural ṭāʾifāt and ṭawāʾif. In al-Qāmūs: "al-ṭāʾifa of a thing is a piece of it, or one and upward, or up to a thousand, or at least two men, or one man, in which case it has the sense of the self." The commentator on al-Qāmūs said in al-Tāj: "His saying 'in which case it has the sense of the self' is a justification for its tāʾ being a feminine marker in that case, i.e. 'the roaming self'. Al-Rāghib said: when a group is meant by ṭāʾifa, it is a plural of ṭāʾif; and when one is meant by it, it may be a plural used figuratively for the one, or it may be like rāwiya and ʿallāma and the like."
(تَفِيءَ) The imperfect of fāʾa, i.e. "he returned".
(أَقْسِطُوا) Be just; from the quadriliteral aqsaṭa, in contrast with the triliteral qasaṭa, whose meaning is to act unjustly. One says qasaṭa al-rajul when he has been unjust and aqsaṭa when he has been just. The Exalted said: «وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا». He said in al-Tāj: "For justice there are two forms, qasaṭa and aqsaṭa; for injustice there is one form, qasaṭa without alif."
(قَوْمٌ) al-qawm: men specifically, because they are the ones who manage the affairs of women. Allah the Exalted said: الرِّجالُ قَوَّامُونَ عَلَى النِّساءِ, and he, peace be upon him, said: "Women are flesh upon a chopping block, except what those who defend defend it", and those who defend are men. In origin it is a plural of qāʾim, like ṣuwwam and zuwwar as plurals of ṣāʾim and zāʾir, or it is named with a maṣdar; from some of the Arabs: "when I eat food I love sleep and dislike qawm", i.e. standing. The restriction of al-qawm to men is explicit in the verse and in the saying of Zuhayr:
وما أدري وسوف أخال أدري ... أقوم آل حصن أم نساء
(I do not know, though I shall presume I know, whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)
As for their saying of the people of Pharaoh and the people of ʿĀd that they are males, the word qawm does not comprise both groups; rather the mention of males was intended and the mention of females left out because they are followers of their men. This is what he stated in al-Kashshāf. So it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning men specifically, and its singular in meaning is rajul; and it was said it is a plural with no singular from its own wording. Some of them said: al-qawm is a group of people, and the plural is aqwām, aqāwim, aqāʾim and aqāwīm; and a man's qawm is his relatives who join with him in one grandfather.
(تَلْمِزُوا) al-lamz is piercing and striking with the tongue. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "lamazahu lamzan, of the pattern ḍaraba, means he found fault with him, and the Seven read it so; and of the pattern qatala it is a dialect form; and its origin is gesturing with the eye and the like."
(تَنابَزُوا) al-tanābuz: the form tafāʿul from al-nabz, which is calling by a nickname; al-nabaz is a nickname of evil. One says tanābazū and tanābazū (two forms) when they call one another by an evil nickname.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ طائِفَتانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما) The waw is a conjunction; إِنْ is conditional; طائِفَتانِ is the agent of an omitted verb that what follows explains; مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ is an adjective of طائِفَتانِ; اقْتَتَلُوا is a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma (the secret of its being attached to the plural waw will come in the section on rhetoric); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis; أَصْلِحُوا is an imperative, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and the waw is the agent; and بَيْنَهُما is an adverbial attached to أَصْلِحُوا.
(فَإِنْ بَغَتْ إِحْداهُما عَلَى الْأُخْرى فَقاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّى تَفِيءَ إِلى أَمْرِ اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إِنْ is conditional; بَغَتْ is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the omitted alif because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; إِحْداهُما is the agent of بَغَتْ; عَلَى الْأُخْرى are both attached to بَغَتْ; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; قاتِلُوا is an imperative, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and the waw is the agent; الَّتِي is a direct object, and the clause تَبْغِي is the ṣila of الَّتِي. حَتَّى is a particle of limit and genitive; تَفِيءَ is an imperfect made accusative by an implied أَنْ after حَتَّى, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she"; and إِلى أَمْرِ اللَّهِ are both attached to تَفِيءَ.
(فَإِنْ فاءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما بِالْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and the i'rab of what follows the fāʾ has preceded; بِالْعَدْلِ is a ḥāl, i.e. "being just"; إِنَّ with its ism, and the clause يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ is its khabar; and the clause of إِنَّ and what follows it is a reason for the command, with no position.
(إِنَّما الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ) إِنَّما is a restraining and restrained particle; الْمُؤْمِنُونَ is a mubtadaʾ and إِخْوَةٌ a khabar. فَأَصْلِحُوا: the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ faṣīḥa); أَصْلِحُوا is an imperative, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and the waw is the agent; and بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ is an adverbial attached to أَصْلِحُوا.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) Conjoined to what preceded; لَعَلَّ with its ism, and the clause تُرْحَمُونَ is its khabar.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ وَلا نِساءٌ مِنْ نِساءٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْراً مِنْهُنَّ) يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: its i'rab has preceded. لا is prohibitive; يَسْخَرْ is an imperfect jussive by the prohibitive lā; قَوْمٌ is the agent; مِنْ قَوْمٍ are both attached to يَسْخَرْ; عَسى is a past verb among the verbs of hope, and here it is complete (tāmma), its ruling to come in the section on benefits; أَنْ and what is within its scope are its agent; خَيْراً is the khabar of يَكُونُوا; مِنْهُمْ are both attached to خَيْرٍ; and وَلا نِساءٌ مِنْ نِساءٍ is conjoined to قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ; the i'rab of عَسى أَنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْراً مِنْهُنَّ has preceded. The clause عَسى أَنْ يَكُونُوا is resumptive, and it comes in the manner of an answer to one inquiring about the reason requiring what he was prohibited.
(وَلا تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَلا تَنابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقابِ) Conjoined to what preceded; its i'rab is clear.
(بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الْإِيمانِ) بِئْسَ is a rigid past verb for the expression of blame; الِاسْمُ is its agent; and الْفُسُوقُ is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm), a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause before it; you may also parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. بَعْدَ الْإِيمانِ, the adverb, is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ) The waw is a conjunction; مَنْ is a jussive-governing conditional noun; لَمْ is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يَتُبْ is an imperfect jussive by لَمْ and is the protasis; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis because it is a nominal sentence; أُولئِكَ is a mubtadaʾ; هُمْ is a separating pronoun with no position, or a second mubtadaʾ; and الظَّالِمُونَ is the khabar of مَنْ or their khabar, the sentence being the khabar of أُولئِكَ; and the clause فَأُولئِكَ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.

* Rhetoric:
1. Construing by meaning: He said اقْتَتَلُوا, whereas the norm would be iqtatalatā, construing by the meaning, because the two groups have the sense of "people" and "folk"; then it was construed by the wording, so He said (بَيْنَهُما).
2. Specification: He singled out the two in mention by His saying «فأصلحوا بين أخويكم» rather than the plural, because the fewest among whom discord occurs is two, so if reconciliation is made binding between the fewest, it is more binding between the more, since the corruption and evil that follow from the discord of a group are greater than in the discord of two.
3. Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: here also is the putting of the overt noun in place of the pronoun, added to those commanded to make peace, for exaggeration in affirmation and exhortation; this device has been pointed out before.
4. The secret of the plural: He did not say "a man at a man" or "a woman at a woman", to announce that more than one of their men and more than one of their women venture upon mockery, and to treat as monstrous the state they were in, and because the scene of the mocker hardly ever lacks someone who amuses himself and laughs at his words and does not come to the prohibition and denunciation due from him, so he becomes a partner of the mocker and his follower in bearing the burden; likewise everyone who finds it pleasant and laughs at it. That leads, even if one began it, to multiplying the mockery and turning the one into a group and a people.

* Benefits:
1. Of the verbs of proximity, ʿasā, ikhlawlaqa and awshaka are distinguished by the permissibility of attributing them to "an yafʿala" when it suffices in place of the khabar, so that they are complete. Ibn Mālik said in al-Khulāṣa:
بعد عسى اخلولق أوشك قد يرد ... غنى بأن يفعل عن ثان فقد
(After ʿasā, ikhlawlaqa and awshaka there may occur "an yafʿala" which suffices in place of the second [element], so it is gone.)
as in «وعسى أن تكرهوا شيئا وهو خير لكم، وعسى أن تحبوا شيئا وهو شر لكم». Two branches rest on this principle. The first: if a noun that is the subject of predication in meaning comes before one of them and "an" with the verb comes after it, as in "Zayd ʿasā an yaqūma", it is permissible to take it as free of a pronoun for that noun, so that ʿasā is attributed to "an" and the verb, which suffice in place of the khabar, and it is complete; this is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. It is also permissible to take it as attributed to the pronoun returning to the noun that precedes it, so that the pronoun is its ism and "an" and the verb are in the position of an accusative as khabar, and it is defective; this is the dialect of Banū Tamīm. To this Ibn Mālik pointed with his saying:
وجرّدن عسى أو ارفع مضمرا ... بها إذا اسم قبلها قد ذكرا
(Strip ʿasā [of a pronoun], or raise a pronoun with it, when a noun has been mentioned before it.)
The revelation came, as in the verse we are dealing with, in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. The second branch: if "an" and the verb immediately follow one of them and a noun that is the subject of predication in meaning comes after it, as in "ʿasā an yaqūma Zaydun", the two preceding views are permissible just as when the subject of predication in meaning came first, and on this view it is a postponed mubtadaʾ and nothing else; two other views are also permissible. One is that it is permissible to take that verb joined to "an" as free of the pronoun returning to the postponed noun, so the verb is attributed to that postponed noun and ʿasā is attributed to "an" and the verb, which suffice in place of the khabar, and it is complete. The second is that the verb is taken as bearing a pronoun for that postponed noun, so the postponed noun is nominative by ʿasā, and "an" and the verb are in the position of an accusative as khabar of ʿasā, fronted before its ism, and it is defective.
2. Discord in Islam: we transmit here a summary of the delightful chapter al-Zamakhsharī devoted to discord in Islam and the duty of the Muslims toward it when it spreads and hardens. He said: "This is an affirmation of what He made binding on whoever undertakes reconciliation between those among the believers between whom discord has occurred, and a statement that faith has established between its people such close connection and clinging kinship that, if it does not surpass brotherhood and stand out above it, it does not fall short of it nor lag behind its extremes. Then, people's custom has been that when something like that arises between two brothers by birth, the rest are bound to rise together to remove and dispel it, and to ride the hard and the easy mount going about with reconciliation and sending envoys between them, until what has frayed of harmony finds one who patches it, and what has worn out of connection finds one who moistens it. So brotherhood in religion is more deserving of that, and of more than that. From the Prophet ﷺ: 'The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him, nor forsake him, nor find fault with him, nor build above him so as to cut the wind from him except with his permission, nor harm him with the smell of his cooking pot.' Then he said: 'Remember it, though only a few of you will remember it.'"
